title: Semaglutide delays 4-hour gastric emptying in women with polycystic ovary syndrome and obesity
authors: Jensterle M, Ferjan S, Ležaič L, Sočan A, Goričar K, Zaletel K, et al.
population: Women with polycystic ovary syndrome and obesity (median BMI 37 kg/m2) randomised to semaglutide 1.0 mg weekly or placebo, single-blind, in Ljubljana
funder: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies; the study was supported by Slovenian Research Agency programme grants P3-0298 and P3-0343, and planning, conduct, interpretation and writing were completely independent of the funder.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
result: By technetium scintigraphy of a solid meal, the reference method, semaglutide retained 37% of the meal in the stomach at 4 hours against no retention on placebo (P = 0.002); half-emptying time was 171 against 118 minutes. Retention rose from baseline by 3.5% at 1 hour, 25.5% at 2 hours, 38.0% at 3 hours and 30.0% at 4 hours. The authors note that earlier semaglutide studies using paracetamol absorption reported no delay or delay only in the first hour.
